MANILA, Philippines – The Department of Health plans to bring funds for the Health Facilities Enhancement Program (HFEP) down to the provincial level in 2027, to speed up infrastructure projects and the decongestion of DOH-run hospitals.

The Senate finance committee recommended an additional P5.4 billion for HFEP, pushing the proposed allocation to P15.58 billion, Senator JV Ejercito said during plenary deliberations on the DOH’s proposed 2027 budget on Friday, November 27.

This comes after the House of Representatives approved only P10.09 billion for HFEP in its version of the general appropriations bill (HGAB), lower than the P14.54 billion allocated in the National Expenditure Program (NEP).

“Admittedly, ‘yong pagiging centralized ay talaga naging problema…for the whole fund to be utilized. Kaya nga po siguro one reason ‘yan [na] P4 billion natanggal sa HGAB,” said Ejercito, the Senate finance committee chairman and the DOH’s budget sponsor.

“But dito sa ating committee, binalik natin dahil may bagong programa ang DOH under Secretary [Edwin] Mercado, that is to download ito sa provincial hospitals and locally-run hospitals. So that they will [be improved, capacitated], para po ma-decongest ‘yong DOH-run hospitals,” he added.

(Admittedly, HFEP being centralized became a problem for the whole fund to be utilized. Maybe that’s one reason why P4 billion was cut from the HGAB. But the Senate finance committee restored it because the DOH, under Secretary Edwin Mercado, has a new program, that is to download the funding to provincial hospitals and locally-run hospitals. So that they will be improved, capacitated, and to decongest the DOH-run hospitals).
With the limited funding, the DOH will also be prioritizing the completion of ongoing HFEP projects, particularly critical health facilities in remote and disadvantaged areas.

Ejercito said DOH-run hospitals, which are end-referral centers providing advanced or specialty care, currently have an average bed occupancy rate of 150%, especially with the implementation of zero balance billing (ZBB).

Since the ZBB rollout in July 2025, 4.2 million patients have benefited from the program in DOH-run hospitals, according to Ejercito. Recently, it was piloted in some hospitals run by local government units (LGUs).

In its version, the Senate realigned P19.8 billion from government assistance programs, including the Medical Assistance Program (MAP) and the Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations or AICS, to augment funding for the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation or PhilHealth.

Ejercito previously said the funds would go directly to hospitals to support the implementation of the ZBB program. This includes P7.6 billion for DOH hospitals, P2 billion for legacy hospitals, and P1 billion for LGU hospitals.

Aside from boosting the HFEP budget, the Senate also provided an additional P1.099 billion for health promotion, P1.599 billion for immunization programs, and P736 million for the Sulu Transition Program.
But if Senator Panfilo Lacson had his way, essential health programs would get even more funds while MAP would become a thing of the past.
MAP, previously called Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially Incapacitated Patients or MAIFIP, has been tagged by watchdogs as “soft pork” and called a “politicized discretionary program.”

Acknowledging that the Senate might have to wrestle with the House regarding unfunding MAP, Lacson suggested introducing a special provision that would allow the remaining P16.2 billion for MAP in the proposed 2027 budget to be allocated to the chambers’ public assistance centers instead. He proposed having DOH personnel oversee the vetting process for claiming the medical aid.
Lacson said this was in a bid to eventually phase out the aid program.

“For next year, the DOH is planning to have a rules-based approach in granting medical assistance to qualified patients. They will, of course, study ‘yong inyong (your) proposal,” Ejercito replied. – Rappler.com
